chapter: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
title: The 'Dixie' man and Harvard students at the Inn
summary: The man who pays $10 for 'Dixie' returns, Whaley makes money from Harvard students, and he jams on Harvard's Gold Coast.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: We used to have this old man, he used to come down here. He was a sharp mother. He must have been five feet, and he'd have a frock coat on--big--and he would come in and, say, --and reach in his pocket and he'd have a billfold and he would whip it out and he'd be looking for a $10 bill. See, he'd give $10 bills, and say, "Play 'Dixie'." And we'd play "Dixie" a couple of times, see, and he'd come back and say "Play 'Dixie,' to give him some more, see, and all the people would do that much; they'd say, "Is that all you know?" and I'd say, "Well, this man's payin' for it!"
So every time he came in he'd give us a $10 bill to play "Dixie" again. Oh, we used to make money! Come in on Monday nights and I'd get off, and hire a taxi--oh, not
a taxi, but a car -- old Packard limousine and we'd go up to the north shore, all around there, and wine and dine and then come back to New York and let the girls go home ... oh yeah.

And the Harvard students, all used to come down that club, and any big night, I'd have my table with my music on it, and some of the Harvard students wouldn't have a table, and I'd say, "Okay, I'll take my music off and tell the waiter to put a napkin or tablecloth on there, and let you sit here" and man, they'd give me money.
Did any of these Harvard kids turn out to be famous that you knew of later?

Charlie Brinkley. He went to Harvard -- I used to go up to the Gold Coast all the time, and they'd have two pianos up there and all the guys would have guitars and everything, and we'd jam every time I'd go up there. Oh, it was a great living up there, I tell you.
